evals.name: focused-debug-turn
evals.prompt: Here is the transcript of a Claude Code session (debug-session.md). Read it, then give me a /tldr.
evals.expected_output: Short scaffolded summary. TL;DR names the actual cause (shared module-level StripeClient) and the outcome (fixed, 50 runs green). Preserves the payments/client.py:88 reference. Keeps the shipping/refunds latent-bug note as unverified in Next. Does not re-investigate.
assertions: Uses the four scaffold headings TL;DR, Did, Found, Next, in that order
The TL;DR line names the actual root cause (shared module-level client / state leaking between tests), not just the topic
The TL;DR line states the outcome: fixed and verified over 50 runs
Preserves at least one clickable file:line reference from the transcript (e.g. payments/client.py:88 or tests/checkout/conftest.py:31)
Mentions the xdist ordering explanation for why CI caught it and local did not
Carries the shipping/refunds latent-bug note forward as an open item, and does not state it as confirmed
Makes no new tool calls beyond reading the transcript file (no grep/test runs against the repo)
Total length is 15 lines or fewer
Opens directly with the summary — no preamble like 'Here is a summary of...'

evals.name: trivial-last-turn-widens
evals.prompt: Read trivial-last-turn.md and /tldr it for me
evals.expected_output: Scope widens past the trivial final exchange ('I created it in this session') to summarise the streaming-export work. Reports the memory numbers and surfaces the partial-response caveat the frontend doesn't handle.
assertions: Uses the four scaffold headings TL;DR, Did, Found, Next, in that order
Scope widens past the trivial final exchange — the summary is about the streaming export work, not about whether bench_export.py existed
The TL;DR line states the outcome with a concrete number (memory dropped to ~84MB, or the 3GB-to-84MB change)
Reports both the memory and the wall-time improvement
Surfaces the streaming-error caveat (partial 200 response / frontend does not check the truncation sentinel) as an open item
Explains the two compounding causes (.all() materialising rows and getvalue() copying the CSV)
Makes no new tool calls beyond reading the transcript file
Total length is 15 lines or fewer
Opens directly with the summary — no preamble

evals.name: long-session-with-bad-news
evals.expected_output: Session-scale recap organised by workstream (auth / rate limiting). Surfaces the blocked Redis decision, the legacy CSRF + open-redirect gap at api/legacy.py:140, and keeps the clock-skew diagnosis hedged as unconfirmed. Under ~20 lines.
assertions: Uses the four scaffold headings TL;DR, Did, Found, Next, in that order
Organises the session by workstream (auth vs rate limiting) rather than replaying turn order
The TL;DR line states both the shipped auth work and that the rate limiter is blocked on a decision
Surfaces the legacy CSRF / open-redirect gap with its api/legacy.py:140 reference
States the Redis vs in-process tradeoff concretely enough to decide on (8 workers enforcing independent limits, resets on deploy)
Keeps the clock-skew diagnosis hedged — does not present it as confirmed root cause
Notes that the rate-limit middleware is written but not wired up
Mentions PR #212 as an open item needing a reviewer
Makes no new tool calls beyond reading the transcript file
Total length is 25 lines or fewer
Does not omit the bad news: blocked decision, unconfirmed diagnosis, and pre-existing security gap all appear
